_about: Automatic Model Room work uses the Luna Codex subscription desk. The queue_targets map is the replacement seam for a future budget-guarded pool dispatcher. Flash starts only through an explicit human bin/flash-on command.

code.instructions: The task is to change a software code repository (fix a bug, add a feature, refactor) so that its tests pass.
code.true: It changes code in a repository.
code.false: It answers a question or produces a document; no repository is changed.

beyond.instructions: The task needs professional judgment or a recommendation, legal or contract interpretation, drafting a document or outreach longer than a short message, design, weighing trade-offs, or reading long documents closely to interpret or summarise what they mean, where a small fast model's mistakes would be costly. Rewording or shortening a few shown sentences does NOT count. Counting or extracting values, however much data, does NOT count: a program handles that.
beyond.true: It needs judgment, interpretation, substantial drafting or design.
beyond.false: It is lookup, arithmetic, extraction, counting or a short rewrite.

script.instructions: Answering needs exact counting, filtering, grouping, joining or arithmetic over data too large to read in full -- a large table, or a folder of many documents where the question is how many or which ones contain something -- so a program must be written and run.
script.true: A program over the data is needed to count, filter or compute.
script.false: No program over large data is needed.

direct.instructions: A capable assistant could answer this correctly in one reply from the question and the short context shown, with no code and no files to read. Rewording, shortening or summarising a few sentences that are shown, arithmetic on numbers that are shown, and pulling a value out of shown text all count as direct.
direct.true: It can be answered in one reply from what is shown.
direct.false: It needs files or folders read, code run, or work beyond one reply.

queue_targets._about: Automatic routes and fallback use Luna. Paid API pools remain excluded until budget admission is enforced by their dispatcher. Flash is reserved for explicit human activation and direct dispatch.

_code_task_origins_about: A Flash code task runs a model-driven agent and its tests on this host, so it is accepted only from these server-derived origins (queue_grammar._origin's channel:actor, never `seat`). Model-posted (mcp:*) code tasks fall back to the configured Codex desk with reason code_origin_untrusted. The run is also sandboxed (tools/room-bridge/flash_wire.py, macOS sandbox-exec); the origin gate is defense in depth, not the only control.

dispatch_targets._about: What a dispatcher (an orchestrator spawning a subagent or queueing a desk) runs for each queue target, via jev_model_route.dispatch(). subagent_model is null for Codex desks. Dispatch through the named Model Room desk rather than starting an in-process Claude agent.

pins._about: Explicit dispatch pins skip Jev unless a sampled audit is requested. An unknown pin name is refused, never routed.

merge_review.reason: Independent review uses Codex while Claude Max agent work is suspended.

gate_authority_code.reason: Gate and authority work uses Codex while Claude Max agent work is suspended.

sol_allowance.reason: Joe asked for Sol desks so the Codex allowance is spent; pinned while that directive stands.

overflow._about: Automatic work stays on the Luna Codex subscription desk when Flash is unavailable.

sonnet.use: rarely: extra turns often cost as much as opus
